The follow-up comparisons of two levels, for more than two conditions

Source: R/followUps.R
topFollowUps.Rd

With more than two conditions (cell method), spicy() tests each pair first with the overall test (are all the condition means equal? overall_p_value, BH-adjusted over the pairs in overall_p_adj). For the pairs that test calls (overall_p_adj at most alpha, R of the m pairs with an overall test), every two levels are then compared: each comparison is the two-condition test of spicy() on the patients of those two levels only (their own between-image and between-patient variances, the same rules for not testing, and the same adjustments). A comparison is tested whenever its two levels pass the rules, even when another level of the pair is too sparse. Within a pair the comparisons are Bonferroni-corrected at the Benjamini-Bogomolov level alpha R / m: a comparison is significant when its p-value is at most p_threshold = alpha R / (m K), K the comparisons tested in the pair. This controls the average, over the pairs called, of the chance of any false comparison within a pair (Benjamini and Bogomolov 2014). Pairs the overall test does not call have no follow-ups.

Usage

topFollowUps(
  x,
  n = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  significant = FALSE,
  figures = NULL
)

Arguments

x

The output from spicy() with more than two conditions.

n

The number of comparisons to list (NULL, the default, lists every one).

from, to

Only the comparisons of pairs with these from and to cell types.

significant

TRUE: only the comparisons significant at the Benjamini-Bogomolov level.

figures

Round to figures significant figures.

Value

A data.frame with one row per called pair and comparison, ordered by the pair's overall p-value and then the comparison's: from, to, the two levels (level_ref, level_comp), the effect in each (excess_ref, excess_comp), their difference (excess_difference, comp minus ref), its standard error, df and p-value, p_threshold, significant, the pair's overall_p_value and overall_p_adj, the number of comparisons tested in the pair (n_comparisons), the frailty variance of the comparison (tau2) and not_tested (why a comparison was not tested; NA when it was). For the allocation effect, the pair's side and the between-image variance of the comparison (tau2_image); with adjustment, adjusted_for and the unadjusted difference and p-value. Row names are "from__to__comp__ref". The same table is x$followUpResults.

References

Benjamini Y, Bogomolov M (2014). Selective inference on multiple families of hypotheses. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B 76(1), 297-318. doi:10.1111/rssb.12028

See also

spicy(), topPairs()

Examples

data("diabetesData")
res <- spicy(diabetesData, condition = "stage", subject = "case", r = 50, from = "Tc", to = c("Th", "beta"))
topFollowUps(res)
#>  [1] from              to                level_ref         level_comp       
#>  [5] excess_ref        excess_comp       excess_difference se               
#>  [9] df                p_value           p_threshold       significant      
#> [13] overall_p_value   overall_p_adj     n_comparisons     tau2             
#> [17] not_tested       
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
